tools.name: get_service_info
tools.description: What this service is, whether payments are available, and on which networks a payment can be made (USDC, x402), with the smallest and largest payment.

tools.name: list_ad_formats
tools.description: The catalog: every ad format (PTC, Sponsored Listing, Banner, Native, Paid Visits, Performance) with its fields, limits, pricing models, minimum bids, minimum order, image, video and HTML5 banner rules and an example order with its price. Read this before building an order.

tools.name: quote_ad
tools.description: Validates an order and returns its exact price in USD with a breakdown. Creates nothing and costs nothing. An invalid order is answered with the code of the problem and the field it is in.

tools.name: create_ad
tools.description: Places an ad order. With an API key whose balance covers the price, it is paid from the balance. Otherwise the result is isError with the x402 PaymentRequired object for the exact price: sign it and call this tool again with the same order and the payment (in _meta["x402/payment"], or as payment_sig

tools.name: buy_ad_credit
tools.description: Buys prepaid ad credit at a fixed price: amount_usd in USDC, 1 USDC = $1.00 of credit (for example 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100). The first call returns isError with the x402 PaymentRequired object; call again with the signed payment. Without an API key the paid result carries api_key: the key of a new acc

tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Creates an anonymous account with a zero balance and returns its API key, shown once. Only needed to upload an image before paying for anything (a Paid Visits ad needs an image or a video); otherwise use buy_ad_credit or create_ad, which create the account with the first payment. A video cannot be u

tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Stores an image for a Paid Visits ad (it needs an image or a video) or a Banner ad (optional; PNG, JPEG or GIF of exactly one banner size, see list_ad_formats) and returns its id, to send as image_id in the order. Needs an API key. A video for a Paid Visits ad is uploaded over HTTP instead: POST the

tools.name: get_video
tools.description: One video of the account: whether it is still processing, in_review or ready (both can be ordered as video_id of a Paid Visits ad), or failed or rejected, with the reason. A video is uploaded over HTTP, not through a tool: POST the file to /api/v1/videos (see list_ad_formats, video of Paid Visits).

tools.name: get_ad
tools.description: One ad of the account: status (in_review, active, paused, rejected, completed, archived), spend, what remains, and the reason if it was rejected.

tools.name: list_ads
tools.description: The account's ads, newest first.

tools.name: get_ad_stats
tools.description: Delivery of one ad: totals and a daily series (impressions, clicks, visits, spend).

tools.name: pause_ad
tools.description: Pauses an active ad (Banner, Native, Paid Visits). Its budget stays reserved.

tools.name: resume_ad
tools.description: Resumes a paused ad: it serves again, within what is left of its budget.

tools.name: archive_ad
tools.description: Ends an ad for good (Banner, Native, Paid Visits). What it has not spent returns to the balance. It cannot be started again.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: The account's balance in USD: available, reserved by ads in review or live, and total.

tools.name: create_event_credential
tools.description: Performance ads. Creates the credential your server signs its conversion events with, and returns credential.key_id (bpk_...), signing_secret_hex and postback_token. They are shown once: store them. The first step of a Performance ad.

tools.name: list_event_credentials
tools.description: Performance ads. The account's event-signing credentials: id, key_id, status and when each was last used. Never the secrets.

tools.name: rotate_event_credential
tools.description: Performance ads. Replaces the secret and the postback token of a credential and returns the new ones, shown once. The old ones keep working for grace_hours (24 unless given, 0 to 168).

tools.name: revoke_event_credential
tools.description: Performance ads. Revokes a credential at once: events signed with it are refused from then on. It cannot be undone.

tools.name: create_sandbox_click
tools.description: Performance ads. Mints a test click (click_id, tclk_...) and a draft_key, to prove the integration before an order. Give destination_template (your https landing URL with {click_id}) for a new ad, or ad_id to test an existing one. Then send one signed test event for the click (send_sandbox_event), a

tools.name: send_sandbox_event
tools.description: Performance ads. With key_id and signing_secret_hex (or postback_token) of your credential, signs a test event for a sandbox click and sends it to the live event endpoint: verified true in the answer means the order will be accepted. Without credentials it only simulates the event against goals and

tools.name: get_sandbox_verification
tools.description: Performance ads. Whether a signed live test event has arrived for a draft_key (before the order) or for an ad: verified, when, by which transport, and the test events seen.

tools.name: update_ad
tools.description: Performance ads. Changes an ad: changes takes the fields of an order that are to change (name, landing_url, ad_title, ad_description, targeting, product_options). An edit that changes what promoters are paid for goes to review again; the answer says so in edit.requires_review.

tools.name: top_up_ad
tools.description: Performance ads. Adds reward budget to an ad; the platform fee is added on top. Paid from the balance, or the result is isError with the x402 PaymentRequired object: sign it and call again with the same arguments, the returned idempotency_key and the payment.

tools.name: end_ad
tools.description: Performance ads. Starts the wind-down of an ad: no new promoters, conversions already attributed are still paid, and what is not spent returns to the balance at the final settlement. It cannot be started again.

tools.name: list_ad_conversions
tools.description: Performance ads. Conversions and daily revenue-share accruals of an ad, newest first: goal, payout, status (held, approved, paid, rejected) and when a hold ends.

tools.name: list_ad_events
tools.description: Performance ads. The events your server sent for an ad, newest first, each with what became of it: accepted, or dropped and why.

tools.name: approve_conversion
tools.description: Performance ads. Approves a conversion that is on hold before its hold ends, which releases its payout to the promoter. It cannot be undone.

tools.name: reject_conversion
tools.description: Performance ads. Rejects a conversion while it is on hold: nothing is paid for it and its amount returns to the ad's budget. reject_code is one of duplicate, fraud, bonus_abuse, chargeback, terms_violation, other; other needs a reject_note of 10 to 500 characters.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_video, get_balance · Private data: create_ad, buy_ad_credit, create_account, upload_image, get_video, create_event_credential, list_event_credentials, rotate_event_credential, revoke_event_credential, send_sandbox_event · Public sink: create_account, upload_image, get_video, create_sandbox_click, send_sandbox_event, list_ad_conversions · Destructive: list_ad_formats.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_video, get_balance · Private data: create_ad, buy_ad_credit, create_account, upload_image, get_video, create_event_credential, list_event_credentials, rotate_event_credential, revoke_event_credential, send_sandbox_event · Public sink: create_account, upload_image, get_video, create_sandbox_click, send_sandbox_event, list_ad_conversions · Destructive: list_ad_formats

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "list_ad_formats" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
